quarterly_data.signal: CFO Mike Stepniak: Honeywell Technologies (per IR, results exclude Honeywell Aerospace after the June 29 spin-off; Quantinuum and pension income removed from adjusted results) grew sales 4% organically in the second quarter; Building Automation +9% organically (segment margin up 90 basis points to 27.1%), Industrial Automation +4% (core business excluding planned divestitures +2%; margin up 90 basis points to 17.2%), Process Automation and Technology -1% (projects +5% on gas, LNG and petrochemicals, aftermarket -6% on a tough comparison with a large catalyst shipment in Q2 2025; margin down 180 basis points to 22.1%). Segment profit increased 9% and segment margin expanded 100 basis points to 19%; adjusted EPS of $1.95 was up 10% (a $0.16 headwind from a higher tax rate); free cash flow was roughly $500 million; roughly $200 million of capital expenditures in the quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 organic sales +4%; segment margin 19% (+100 basis points); adjusted EPS $1.95 (+10%); free cash flow roughly $500 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Vimal Kapur: orders grew 16% organically in the second quarter with broad-based demand across all segments and double-digit short-cycle orders growth in every segment; book-to-bill was 1.1 and ending backlog rose 9%. Process Automation and Technology orders were up 24% organically, led by roughly 50% orders growth in process technology (book-to-bill above 1.2; LNG demand globally the biggest driver); core Industrial Automation orders grew 11% (7% sequentially) with sensing and industrial measurement orders up over 20%; Building Automation orders grew 13%, with over 50% orders growth and 30% organic sales growth in high-growth verticals (data center, hospitality, healthcare) and approximately 30% orders growth in fire. Middle East orders grew over 50% (primarily a few big process technology deals, including LNG facilities); CFO: Middle East revenue expected up about high single digits this year with orders about 40%.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 organic orders +16%; book-to-bill 1.1; ending backlog +9%; PA&T orders +24%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Mike Stepniak: Honeywell raised its 2026 outlook - organic sales growth now 3%-4% (previously 2%-3%), second half 4%-6% (previously 3%-5%); Building Automation mid-single-digit plus, Process Automation and Technology accelerating to high single digits in the second half, Process Automation and Technology and Industrial Automation each now up low single digits for the year (from roughly flat); segment margin expansion of 250-290 basis points, exiting the year above 22% segment margin; adjusted EPS of $8.20 at the midpoint, up approximately 27% (previous midpoint $8.10); free cash flow of roughly $2 billion with approximately 95% conversion; repositioning around $100 million-$110 million for the year. CFO: 'I also think there is more room... to beat even the raised guidance', and 2027 'is looking stronger'. The early close of the Productivity Solutions and Services and Warehouse and Workflow Solutions divestitures (by early August) reduced the 2026 revenue expectation by approximately $400 million.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 organic growth 3%-4% (2H 4%-6%); segment margin +250-290 basis points; adjusted EPS $8.20 midpoint; free cash flow roughly $2 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Vimal Kapur: in LNG Honeywell supplies proprietary equipment (heat exchangers) rather than licensing technology, with typical delivery times of two to three years - orders booked in 2026 convert in 2028, with revenue recognised on a percentage-of-completion basis. CFO Mike Stepniak: 'we're sold out LNG for the next three years'; CEO: 'Totally sold out'.
quarterly_data.figure: LNG sold out for the next three years; two to three year delivery times

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Vimal Kapur: on Quantinuum, Honeywell supported the Quantinuum team in its June initial public offering and expects 'to provide more color on our plans of our 47% ownership stake by early next year'; 'We remain strong supporters of Raj and his team and are excited to be shareholders'. Quantinuum's results have been removed from Honeywell's adjusted results in all prior and future periods.

CEO Vimal Kapur: Honeywell closed the acquisition of the Johnson Matthey Catalyst Technologies business on July 17, joining Process Automation and Technology and adding licensing technologies in hydrogen, methanol and ammonia where Honeywell had no capability, complementary to Honeywell UOP's refining, petrochemicals and renewable fuels offerings; Honeywell also completed the separation of Honeywell Aerospace (June 29). CFO Mike Stepniak: Honeywell's own catalyst business should be up 25%-30% in the second half versus the first half, with a sharp growth inflection in Process Automation and Technology from the third quarter on backlog conversion and much stronger catalyst shipments.

CEO Vimal Kapur on data centers: the data-center build-out has grown beyond the U.S. across Europe and Asia; more data centers are putting in on-site power generation, letting Process Automation automate the utilities, energy storage and incoming gas for those power plants (multiple proposals, none yet in orders); Building Automation benefits from fire detection, security and building management systems; and sensing for liquid cooling is an emerging longer-term opportunity - 'Our sensors are required as a critical input for liquid cooling. All those OEs are actively working with us'. Data centers were about 5% of the Building Automation business three or four years back and he expects a higher number across Honeywell over time.
quarterly_data.figure: data centers about 5% of Building Automation three or four years back

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Mike Stepniak: price was about 3.5%, 3.7% in the second quarter and will be around 4% in the second half, covering inflation, but 'inflation is stubborn' - 'We see a lot of inflation in electronics, memory, obviously copper, and we also see inflation in labor'; most margin expansion comes from productivity, stranded cost takeout and new product introductions rather than price-cost. Stranded cost is about $20 million better than the roughly $85 million year-end figure given at Investor Day; Honeywell should enter 2027 with about $60 million-$65 million of stranded cost to eliminate early next year.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 price about 3.5%, 3.7%; 2H price around 4%; stranded cost entering 2027 about $60 million-$65 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Vimal Kapur: Honeywell Forge software (all AI-based offerings) ARR is expected to grow about 15% in 2026, from about $900 million to a little over $1 billion, driven by deeper penetration of existing offerings and new Forge launches; Honeywell needs to deliver the same 15% in 2027. Industrial Automation delivery performance has risen from the mid-40s at the start of the year toward a high-80% target, new products drove 10% Industrial Automation orders growth, and the segment saw a lot of growth in semiconductor fabs; CFO: Industrial Automation should reach a 22% margin rate in the fourth quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: Forge ARR growth about 15% in 2026 (about $900 million to a little over $1 billion)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Vimal Kapur: three-year targets from the June 11 Investor Day - approximately $12 of adjusted EPS (by 2029, organic only, no M&A assumed), more than 10% growth annually, over 200 basis points of margin expansion from stranded cost removal, Industrial Automation portfolio actions and the aerospace trademark agreement plus 60 basis points a year of operational margin expansion, the 24% target, which the CFO said in June is achievable, and free cash flow conversion above 90% (line of sight to 95% in the second half of 2026). M&A of $1 billion-$5 billion enterprise value is to be viewed from 2027 onwards.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $12 adjusted EPS by 2029; 24% margin target; free cash flow conversion over 90%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Vimal Kapur on the Middle East conflict: guidance assumes conditions stay as they are, with no improvement and no significant escalation or further supply-chain disruption; Honeywell lost some revenue in Q1 and Q2 when customer sites closed in March and April, collection issues are 'modest, they are not material'; customers are diversifying process investment beyond the Middle East - a large project in Africa (partly booked) and downstream refining and petrochemical investment in Asia - and Middle East investment is pivoting toward logistics infrastructure.
